derived_results.claim: For an exact Gaussian split, the two-sample GLR lower tail can be evaluated from three independent sufficient statistics without the r69 rectangular mean/variance relaxation.
derived_results.statement: Normalize P=N(0,1), Q=N(mu,r), with scored sample sizes m and n. Let A~chi-square(m-1), B=r*chi-square(n-1), independently. Let sigma_D^2=1/m+r/n, lambda_nc=mu^2/sigma_D^2 and c=(mn/(m+n))*sigma_D^2=(n+mr)/(m+n). Then C=c*Z with Z~noncentral-chi-square_1(lambda_nc), independent of A,B. The exact separate-vs-pooled Gaussian GLR is G=(m+n)/2 log((A+B+C)/(m+n)) - m/2 log(A/m) - n/2 log(B/n). Therefore F_G(q)=E_{A,B}[F_ncx2(((m+n) exp((2q+m log(A/m)+n log(B/n))/(m+n))-A-B)_+/c;1,lambda_nc)]. This is an exact distributional identity under the stated Gaussian alternative; only the numerical integration of the outer expectation is approximate.

derived_results.claim: Numerical integration of the exact GLR representation continues to place the finite-sample lower-tail worst direction at the pure variance-increase endpoint for all three r70 scales, matching the population theorem rather than the r69 mixed-direction box artifact.
derived_results.details: Using 61 log-spaced variance ratios over each complete normalized KL level, scored sizes m=T-16,n=H-16, and scrambled-Sobol outer integration with exact conditional noncentral-chi-square CDF, the beta_G lower quantile was minimized at r=r_+(I), mu=0 in all three cases. Endpoint repeated integrations with six independent 2^16 Sobol scrambles varied by only about 0.003-0.005 nats. This is strong numerical evidence over the scanned level, not a continuum stochastic-order theorem.

derived_results.claim: Replacing only the GLR part of r69 by its exact alternative lower quantile yields a much tighter prospective 1-beta certificate while retaining the explicit SNML/overfit and PFA accounting.
derived_results.statement: Split beta=0.10 into beta_G for the exact GLR lower quantile q_G(beta_G) and beta_D=beta-beta_G for the four MLE-overfit terms. With epsilon=beta_D/8, use the existing exact Gaussian K(q,epsilon) bounds for scored pre/post and the two burn-ins. Then, with probability at least 1-beta, log C >= q_G(beta_G)-K(m,epsilon)-K(n,epsilon)-2K(16,epsilon)-r_16(T)-r_16(H). Dependence between G and the overfit terms is harmless because the events are combined only by a union bound.

derived_results.claim: At the existing r70 activation/lifetime settings, the hybrid certificate clears the first-candidate PFA threshold over the scanned full KL level by large margins instead of failing by 8-10 nats as the old box certificate did.
derived_results.setup: alpha=0.05, beta=0.10, burn-in 16, equal scale mass 1/3, first local start mass pi_1=0.3690702464, threshold log[1/(alpha*(1/3)*pi_1)]=5.091112846 nats. Numerical beta_G was optimized on a fine grid at the variance-up endpoint.
derived_results.scope: Exact candidate split; well-specified Gaussian pre/post laws; numerical integration error is not included in the formal probability budget, so these values are a prospective numerical certificate candidate rather than a machine-verified theorem.

derived_results.claim: Under the same hybrid numerical certificate, the three lifetimes can be cut from 384/512/768 to 176/288/448 while keeping original activations and spacings, reducing individualized state from 52 to 27 for exact splits.
derived_results.interpretation: The I=1 scale is close to the numerical certificate boundary, so no state reduction should be adopted until integration error and split-misalignment are incorporated into a rigorous margin. The 27-state figure is a design lead, not a finalized guarantee.

derived_results.claim: The proposed shorter lifetimes retained a very large empirical exact-SNML margin under sampled first-grid-interval misalignment at the pure variance-up direction, suggesting that formal misalignment tightening is likely to fit inside the recovered certificate slack.
derived_results.details: For each scale, the true changepoint was placed at 9 evenly spaced positions between the first two candidate starts; both neighboring candidates were simulated with exact conditional-SNML evidence, 6000 paths per position, and their own pi_1/pi_2 PFA thresholds. At H={176,288,448}, the worst sampled better-neighbor 10th-percentile margin was about 28.08, 29.06 and 27.51 nats respectively. The worst sampled positions were x=12 of 16, x=20 of 32 and x=32 of 64. This is engineering evidence only; it does not replace a 1-beta contaminated-segment certificate and did not scan the entire KL direction continuum.

candidates_new.mechanism: Use the exact three-statistic alternative GLR distribution for the power part of a candidate certificate, retaining separate exact SNML regret and conservative MLE-overfit charges, instead of lower-bounding mean/variance ingredients independently.
candidates_new.evidence: Exact distributional reduction plus stable numerical integration and agreement of the scanned finite-sample worst direction with the r70 population theorem.
candidates_new.confidence: high for the distributional identity; medium-high for the numerical design values until integration is rigorously bounded.

candidates_new.mechanism: Keep T0 and g fixed but shorten H to {176,288,448}, for 27 individualized states total, if a rigorous misalignment-aware certificate confirms the numerical margins.
candidates_new.evidence: Hybrid exact-split numerical certificate plus large exact-SNML misalignment engineering margins.
candidates_new.confidence: medium; not yet adoption-grade because the I=1 exact-split numerical margin is only about 0.023 nats above threshold and no rigorous quadrature/misalignment error budget has been added.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: The r69 rectangular mean/variance certificate should be retained because it is already rigorous.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: It is valid but badly capacity-inefficient in this regime. The exact GLR lower-tail representation shows tens of nats of recoverable slack and removes the mixed-direction artifact numerically.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: The 27-state design is already formally certified.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Rejected. The GLR CDF identity is exact, but the present outer integration is numerical and split misalignment is only Monte Carlo-checked. In particular the I=1 shorter lifetime has very little numerical formal margin after the conservative overfit/SNML charges.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: The finite-sample worst Gaussian direction at fixed KL has now been proved to be pure variance increase.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Not yet. It is proved only for the population GLR (r70); r71 adds a dense full-level finite-sample numerical lower-tail scan with the same minimizer, not a stochastic-order proof over the continuum.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: Neighbor-misalignment Monte Carlo can replace a contaminated-segment certificate.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Rejected. It only shows substantial empirical slack in the tested pure variance-up first-grid interval and is useful for prioritizing proof effort.

frontier: Turn the exact conditional-CDF identity into a rigorously error-bounded numerical lower quantile, for example with deterministic quadrature plus interval/error control or a conservative randomized integration confidence bound. The I=1 27-state lead especially needs an explicit numerical-error margin.

Derive the contaminated-segment GLR/SNML certificate for the two neighboring candidates. A late candidate has d Q observations in its scored pre segment; an early candidate has max(x-b,0) P observations in its scored post segment. Use the independent homogeneous subgroup means/within-SSE decomposition to represent each contaminated sample variance as within-group chi-squares plus a between-group noncentral square, then control its dependence with the segment mean difference.

After the two-neighbor 1-beta certificate exists, re-optimize T0,g,H,scale weights under a total state budget and compare the 27-state candidate against the old 52-state bank with an explicit safety margin rather than merely crossing threshold numerically.

Seek a finite-sample stochastic-order argument showing that the lower tail of the exact Gaussian GLR is minimized at the variance-up endpoint along a fixed KL level. If unavailable, certify the continuum by interval subdivision and monotone/numerically bounded envelopes rather than a point grid.

Quantify the separable candidate-wise null-infimum penalty versus the shared-null infimum-after-sum detector after the single-candidate certificate is tightened, so memory optimization is not performed against a materially weaker objective.
Do not generalize this Gaussian certificate to heavy tails or non-Gaussian alternatives without a separately valid robust class.
exact_next_action: Build a rigorous contaminated-segment representation for one late and one early neighboring candidate using homogeneous subgroup sufficient statistics. For each candidate, express every required segment sum, sample mean and SSE from independent group-level normals and chi-squares, then derive a conservative 1-beta lower bound on exact conditional-SNML log C that preserves the covariance between contaminated SSE and segment mean rather than using an independent rectangle. Evaluate the better of the two neighbors for every changepoint offset x in [0,g] and the full Gaussian KL level. In parallel, replace scrambled-Sobol point estimates for the exact-split GLR quantile with a numerically error-bounded integration so the 27-state lead can either receive a real margin or be rejected.
